_comment: Performance interventions applied by kPerfInterventions (apps/wpe/WPEUserScripts.h),
loaded by WPEWebPage and gated on ATLANTIC_PERF_INTERVENTIONS.
Everything here DELAYS work; nothing here drops it. Blocking is the adblocker's
job and it has a filter list behind it — this file exists for the work a page
legitimately asks for and the user never sees.
Shipped at /usr/share/atlantic-browser/perf-interventions.json. The loader
prefers a newer copy in the adblock cache dir, so the same weekly gh-pages
refresh that carries engine.dat can carry this file later without a rebuild.
Fields:
defaults.deferScripts   hold matching JS-inserted third-party scripts
defaults.lazyImages loading=lazy + decoding=async on untagged
defaults.lazyFrames     loading=lazy on untagged <iframe>
defaults.pauseAnims     pause infinite CSS animations outside the viewport
defaults.eagerImages    images left eager, in document order, to protect LCP
deferPatterns           substrings matched against a script's src
deferUntil.idleMs       release deadline after window load; a user gesture
always releases first
sites[].match           hostname or parent domain
sites[].disable/enable  intervention names to force off/on for that site
sites[].defer           extra defer patterns for that site
sites[].eagerImages     per-site LCP budget
sites[].css             per-site 'lite' stylesheet (appended to the page)

sites._why: Style resolution dominates these two profiles (34% / 44%); every byte of third-party JS competes with it on the main thread. One eager image: both lead with a single hero.
